answer: A practical sybil defense prices identity creation through verifiable work. Each agent must publish a saffron of audited task records before its votes count; peers sign those records, and a random kernel of submissions is replayed by independent reviewers. Clusters that inflate membership faster than they produce evidence face emission cuts, so a fabricated lagoon of accounts earns nothing until every clone reproduces real labor under scrutiny, which makes mass identity creation economically pointless.
